Location: Harar, Ethiopia

I’m Henok Tsegaye, born and based in Harar, Ethiopia, the “City of Saints,” known for its ancient walls, vibrant markets, and unique traditions.

Read more

Step through one of the five ancient gates and you leave the modern world behind. Inside the 16th-century walls of Harar Jugol — a UNESCO World Heritage Site — hundreds of winding alleyways twist past more than 80 mosques and shrines, and houses painted in every shade of blue, yellow, pink and green light up the old town at every corner.

Here the day starts with the smell of freshly roasted coffee and ends with one of Africa's most unforgettable sights: wild hyenas fed by hand at night, a tradition unique to Harar. In between, you can wander the buzzing Harari market, watch women weave colorful baskets, and follow the footsteps of the poet Arthur Rimbaud, who once called this city home.

Harar is not a place you just visit — it is a place you feel, taste and remember for life. And I would love to show it to you like a local friend, not just a guide.

Inside Harar

Jegol is a living museum, a UNESCO World Heritage site inside ancient 16th-century stone walls, with more than 360 narrow, colourful alleys and sacred shrines tucked into every quarter.

$40
6–8 hrsEntrance fees not included
1/5

Jegol Old City

A historic walled city with over 360 narrow, colourful alleys, sacred shrines and traditional Islamic architecture.

“Step back in time amidst vibrant alleyways echoing centuries of Islamic scholarship, trade heritage, and spiritual devotion.”

Sherif Harar City Museum

A cultural museum about the unique history of the Harari people.

“Houses an exceptional collection of ancient manuscripts, traditional coinage, and royal artifacts offering deep historical context.”

Rimbaud's House & Museum

A striking traditional residence dedicated to the French poet Arthur Rimbaud.

“Blends French colonial legacy with classic Harari architectural design and literary exhibits.”
1/2

Harari Cultural Centre - አዳ ጋር

An authentic showcase of the domestic architecture and interior design of the Harar highlands.

“Features meticulously arranged display shelves laden with heirloom basketry and imported porcelain against vibrant interior colors.”
1/3

Sugiya Tera Market

A sensory overload where the region's rich aromatic heritage comes alive.

“Immerse yourself in towering mounds of colorful local spices, dried herbs, and incense amidst the vibrant commercial banter of local traders.”

Falcon Feeding Site

Another unusual Harar encounter: watch local feeders call wild birds of prey down to take meat from the hand, a close-up wildlife moment right in the city.

1/2

Hyena Feeding Site

A legendary night-time spectacle unique to Harar, where wild hyenas are hand-fed by local “hyena men”.

“Witness an extraordinary centuries-old tradition of peaceful coexistence as powerful wild predators accept meat directly under the cover of dusk.”

Villages, Markets & Farms Around Harar

Rural landscapes, desert markets and farming traditions beyond the city walls.

$140–$160
Depends on your interest · 6–8 hrsIncludes two-way transportation, tour guide, camel market and village entrance fees.
1/16

Koremi (Koromi) Village: the living ancestor of Harar

  • The primordial blueprint: an untouched ancient settlement said to predate Harar itself and to be the original model of the walled city.
  • A timeless architectural echo: winding streets and historic homes built in the same style that later inspired the alleys of Harar.
  • A journey back in time: a rural sanctuary little changed by modern development, where ancestral traditions and village life carry on.
1/5

Babile Camel Market & Stone Marvels

  • The desert's majestic fleet: a lively, dusty market where hundreds of dromedary camels gather for nomadic trade.
  • Nature's sculpture garden: wind and time have carved tall, gravity-defying rock pillars and balanced stones.
  • Dramatic badland views: sweeping landscapes of rock spires, gorges and wide horizons.
1/2

Aweday

The largest khat market in the world, working at a frantic pace day and night.

“A massive logistical powerhouse where tons of fresh green stimulant leaves are traded internationally every single day.”
1/2

Khat origin of Aweday / Mume Ame Khat Farm

Wide terraced farms growing Ethiopia's famous green cash crop.

“Tour lush, terraced hillsides to learn about the intricate cultivation, harvesting, and socio-economic landscape of the Harar highlands.”

Special destination: Kundudo Mountain

A flat-topped mountain east of Harar, known for its herd of wild horses and wide views over the highlands.

Ask for a price
Duration on requestMessage me with your dates and group size and I will send the price and plan.
  • Wild horses: a rare herd of feral horses lives on the mountain.
  • A flat-topped mountain: a classic Ethiopian amba rising above the Harar countryside.
  • Panoramic views: sweeping views over the surrounding valleys and plateaus.
  • Getting there: about 1.5 hours by road from Harar.
